title: Jota wins Imola after Newblood stops in the closing minutes
dek: Simon Dolan, Harry Tincknell and Filipe Albuquerque won the 4 Hours of Imola from pole in the Jota Zytek after Christian Klien's leading Morgan stopped in the final minutes.

chapters.title: A 38-car field and a new tyre deal
text: The second round of the 2014 European Le Mans Series, the 4 Hours of Imola on 18 May, came a month after the Silverstone opener and two weeks before the Le Mans test day, so every LMP2 team on the entry list also had the 24 Hours in mind. The field was cut to 38 cars when Larbre Competition and the Sebastien Loeb Racing Audi withdrew. The Loeb team kept its Oreca in the series.

Thiriet by TDS Racing arrived as Silverstone winners and championship leaders, and as the winners of the previous year's Imola race, with Pierre Thiriet, Ludovic Badey and Tristan Gommendy still in their Morgan-Nissan #46. Jota Sport came looking for redemption after a dominant Silverstone ended with a single point for pole, the Zytek having crashed out of the lead. Filipe Albuquerque, the Audi factory driver on loan, rejoined Simon Dolan and Harry Tincknell. Tincknell had never raced at Imola.

The biggest technical story concerned the reigning champions. Signatech Alpine announced the Monday before the race that it was swapping Michelin for Dunlop tyres for the rest of the season, without any testing, which left Loeb Racing's Oreca #24 as the only Michelin-shod LMP2 car in the field. Murphy Prototypes made a late change of its own, putting Nathanael Berthon, fresh from a strong Paul Ricard test, into its Oreca alongside Rodolfo Gonzalez and Karun Chandhok in place of the previously announced Alex Kapadia. Greaves Motorsport ran a two-driver crew, as Chris Dyson was absent on business.

chapters.title: Albuquerque clear by 0.684s
text: Practice had suggested a close fight. Murphy Prototypes led the first session on Saturday morning with a 1:36.337, and in the second Nelson Panciatici put the Dunlop-shod Alpine on top with a 1:35.318, only 0.095s ahead of the Jota Zytek, with just 0.509s covering the top five. Panciatici's lap came in the closing minutes, when most cars had pitted and the track was clear, and four red flags had interrupted the session.

Qualifying on Sunday morning was decisive. Panciatici, Gommendy and Albuquerque traded the top spot late in the 20-minute session before Albuquerque took pole with a 1:33.974, 0.684s clear of Gommendy's 1:34.658. It was Jota's second pole in as many races, with Tincknell having claimed the one at Silverstone, and the Portuguese driver said the grid slot would matter because traffic on the circuit was heavy. Gommendy had held provisional pole and aborted a later lap after outbraking himself at Variante Alta.

Panciatici was third on 1:34.861, only 0.021s ahead of Berthon, who set his fastest time on his first qualifying run for the Murphy car. Christian Klien was fifth for Newblood by Morand Racing on 1:35.593, a little disappointed, ahead of Franck Mailleux's Race Performance Oreca, Tom Kimber-Smith's Greaves Zytek, Julien Schell's Pegasus Morgan and Vincent Capillaire in the Loeb Oreca. Albuquerque admitted that the Ferraris of the GTE field pulled away on the straights, so the prototypes would have few chances to pass them cleanly.

chapters.title: Tincknell holds off the Alpine
text: Tincknell started the Jota car and held the lead through the opening stint against Panciatici's Signatech Alpine #36, working through the traffic. Gonzalez ran third for a stage in the Murphy Oreca. Of the other front-runners, Badey started for Thiriet, Gary Hirsch for Newblood, Matthew McMurry for Greaves and Capillaire for Loeb.

chapters.title: Jota slips back, then fights through
text: Dolan, who as the silver-rated driver had to complete at least 2h20m behind the wheel, took over and defended the lead against Paul-Loup Chatin until a slip at Piratella let the Alpine through. A trip through the gravel at Acque Minerale then left his tyres clogged with pick-up, and the Thiriet Morgan and Hirsch in the Newblood Morgan #43 moved ahead. Jota had been saving fuel since the start to keep its strategy flexible, and with Albuquerque in the car the Zytek came straight back into contention.

After 2h35m a Safety Car was called for damage at Acque Minerale, bunching the field into what became an 80-minute sprint. The Murphy Oreca had already retired in the third hour with gearbox failure, so Gonzalez's early challenge was over. Dolan thought the neutralisation hurt Jota, because rivals who needed a late splash of fuel no longer had to stop for it.

chapters.title: Three cars in the lead fight
text: The restart set up a three-way battle for the lead between Newblood, Thiriet and Jota, with Gommendy running a few seconds behind Dolan. Kimber-Smith was the quickest car on the track for Greaves in the closing stages, and McMurry, aged 16, had driven a 2h25m stint without trouble earlier on. Signatech, with Chatin at the wheel, had to make a late stop because of the Safety Car, ending its chance to challenge for the win.

chapters.title: Klien passes Dolan, then stops
text: With about 20 minutes left Klien lined up Dolan at Tamburello and took the lead, the Austrian giving the Englishman just enough room on the inside. Dolan said he settled for second until he saw an LMP2 stationary at the exit of the corner. It was the Morgan, which had stopped with no oil pressure and a mechanical problem within the last five minutes, after the car had led most of the race.

Thiriet's chance had already gone. Brake problems sent Gommendy to the pits in the final hour and dropped the Morgan to fifth, two laps down. Dolan took the flag 28.869s clear of Capillaire and Jan Charouz, who had a quiet race and were rewarded for it with second place, in only their second event with the Oreca. Signatech Alpine finished third, a further 13.8s back, with Chatin, Panciatici and Oliver Webb. Kimber-Smith and McMurry came home fourth, a lap down, and Newblood was not classified.

chapters.title: Redemption for Jota, heartbreak for Newblood
text: Dolan, Tincknell and Albuquerque took 25 points plus two for pole, and Jota moved up to second in the LMP2 standings on 27, behind Badey, Gommendy and Thiriet on 35. Dolan was happy to see the win after losing the lead late at Silverstone, saying he felt no sympathy for the driver in front because the same thing had happened to Jota a month earlier. It had been his best race to date, after he recovered from his early errors.

At Newblood by Morand Racing, Klien was crushed. He said he had received no warning from the car, no light and nothing on the data, and that he suspected an oil pump failure, while the team would not know for sure until it was back at the factory. He had been in control and double-stinted the soft tyre as a gamble. Hirsch and Brandela had laid the foundation for what looked like a certain victory.

Behind Jota, Loeb Racing took the runner-up spot with the only Michelin-shod car, and Signatech Alpine reached the podium on its first weekend with Dunlop. Pegasus Racing took sixth, two laps down. Dolan was also critical of the speed difference between the GT cars and the prototypes, saying that a Ferrari travelling about 15 km/h faster on the straights was dangerous.

Thiriet by TDS Racing had run its last race with the Morgan-Nissan, with the Ligier JS P2 due to make its debut at Le Mans in June and to replace the Morgan in the ELMS from the Red Bull Ring on 20 July, the next round. Greaves Motorsport confirmed that Kimber-Smith and McMurry would be joined by Dyson in its Le Mans line-up.

facts.v: Filipe Albuquerque put the Jota Zytek on pole with a 1:33.974, 0.684s ahead of Gommendy's Morgan.
